entries.title: Lamentations 4:1
segments:
How is the gold become dim! how is the glory of Jerusalem, and the honor in which her people were once held, turned to shame. 
 
vv 1-2. 
 
They who honor God by obeying his commands, shall be exalted by him to true honor and strength; but all who despise him, and trample under foot his law, he will make weak and contemptible before their fellow men.

entries.title: Lamentations 4:3
segments: Is become cruel; hunger has driven her to cruel deeds.

entries.title: Lamentations 4:5
segments: The ease and frequency with which God's judgments reach the high and luxurious, reducing them to a condition of extreme want and wretchedness, ought to be a warning to all parents against the common error of bringing up children in habits of luxury and self-indulgence. Such habits not only tempt to sin in many ways, but disqualify them for the endurance of those hardships which, amid the many vicissitudes of life, will very probably fall to their lot.

entries.title: Lamentations 4:7
segments: Nazarites; persons specially consecrated or set apart.  For the law of the Nazarites, see
.  They were in high honor with the people, and paid especial attention to purity of person.

entries.title: Lamentations 4:10
segments: The unnatural cruelty to which the horrors of famine so often impelled Jewish mothers, was a striking fulfilment of God's prophetic denunciations by Moses,
; at the same time it showed the weakness of mere natural affection to resist the pressure of extreme suffering.

entries.title: Lamentations 4:14
segments:
They have wandered; the prophets and priests, with the people whom they had seduced into sin. 
 
  With blood; the blood of the people of Jerusalem slaughtered by the enemy to avenge the righteous blood which they had shed.  Compare
.  The city was so filled with this, that the living could not avoid polluting their garments with it.

entries.title: Lamentations 4:15
segments:
They cried; all whom they met. 
 
  Depart ye; that is, keep at a distance from us as unclean. 
 
  Fled away and wandered; from their own land into captivity. 
 
  Sojourn there; dwell in their own land.

entries.title: Lamentations 4:16
segments: They respected not; that is, the enemy.

entries.title: Lamentations 4:20
segments:
The breath of our nostrils, the anointed of the Lord; our king.  He is called the breath of their nostrils because their life as a nation is bound up in his. 
 
  Taken in their pits; like a wild beast.

Under his shadow--among the heathen; there had been two previous capitivities, and many of the Jews were already dispersed among the heathen.  So long as Zedekiah remained at peace with Nebuchadnezzar, they trusted to his influence to secure them from oppression.

entries.title: Lamentations 4:21
segments:
Rejoice and be glad; that is, if thou wilt; but thy joy shall be short. 
 
  The cup; the cup of God's wrath. 
 
vv 21-22. 
 
God chastises his own people for their profit, not for their destruction; the calamities that come upon them will be in due time overpast; but the enemies of Zion, who desire her destruction, and rejoice in her misfortunes, shall fall to rise no more.

entries.title: Lamentations 4:22
segments: Is accomplished; that is, shall soon be accomplished.
